prompt: Which species has a central atom with an incomplete octet (only 6 electrons)?
explain: In BF₃, boron has only 3 bond pairs, so 6 electrons: electron-deficient.

prompt: Which of these is an odd-electron molecule, which violates the octet rule?
explain: NO₂ has 17 valence electrons, an odd number, so one electron is unpaired.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of these can NOT be explained by the octet rule?
explain: The octet rule gives no information on molecular shape or relative stability/energy.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of electrons around Xe in the Lewis structure of XeF₂ is
explain: Xe has 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs: 10 electrons, an expanded octet.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In H₂ formation, each hydrogen atom attains the electronic configuration of
explain: Hydrogen completes a duplet (1s²) by sharing, like helium; the octet rule does not apply.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of lone pairs on the central atom I in the Lewis structure of I₃⁻ is
explain: I₃⁻ central I has 2 bond pairs + 3 lone pairs (10 electrons, expanded octet).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which species has an expanded octet on its central atom?
explain: S in SF₆ has 12 electrons; the others have 8 around the central atom.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which molecule has an incomplete octet on the central atom, besides being electron-deficient?
explain: Be in BeCl₂ has only 4 electrons around it, while the others have expanded octets.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The Born–Haber cycle for lattice enthalpy is an application of which law?
explain: Born–Haber cycle uses Hess's law: enthalpy of formation equals the sum of the steps in the cycle.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Lattice enthalpy (NCERT convention) is the energy needed to do which of the following?
options: Convert one mole of solid into gaseous atoms
Separate one mole of solid into gaseous ions
Hydrate one mole of gaseous ions
Remove one electron from the gaseous cation
explain: Lattice enthalpy = energy to completely separate one mole of solid ionic compound into gaseous ions (positive value).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which factor mainly compensates for the high second ionisation enthalpy of Mg in forming MgCl₂?
explain: The extra lattice enthalpy released by Mg²⁺ more than compensates for the second IE, so MgCl₂ is stable.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why is NaCl₂ (containing Na²⁺) not formed?
options: Second IE of Na is extremely high
Cl₂ bond enthalpy is too high
explain: Removing an electron from the noble-gas core of Na⁺ needs very high energy, which lattice enthalpy cannot repay.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which pair of conditions favours the formation of an ionic bond?
options: Low IE, high negative electron gain enthalpy
explain: Easy cation formation, easy anion formation and high lattice enthalpy favour ionic bonding.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Ionic solids are brittle because of which reason?
options: Layer shift brings like ions together, repelling
explain: A displaced layer brings like charges face to face, and the repulsion cleaves the crystal.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: A salt dissolves in water when the following condition holds:
explain: The energy released on hydrating the ions must overcome the lattice enthalpy for the salt to dissolve.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which alkali metal fluoride is the least soluble in water?
explain: LiF has very high lattice enthalpy, which hydration enthalpy cannot overcome, so it is sparingly soluble.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which step of the Born–Haber cycle for NaCl(s) is exothermic besides lattice formation?
explain: Cl(g) + e⁻ → Cl⁻(g) releases energy; sublimation, ionisation and bond dissociation are endothermic.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why do ionic compounds conduct electricity in the molten state but not as solids?
explain: In the solid the ions are fixed in the lattice; on melting or dissolving they become free to move.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The ionic bond is described as which of these?
explain: Coulombic attraction acts equally in all directions, so each ion is surrounded by oppositely charged ions.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Among LiCl, NaCl, KCl, which has the most covalent character, according to Fajans' rules?
explain: The small, highly polarising Li⁺ distorts the Cl⁻ cloud most, giving the most covalent character.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Second electron gain enthalpy of oxygen (O⁻ → O²⁻) is:
explain: Adding e⁻ to an anion is repelled; metal oxides still form because lattice enthalpy compensates.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which sodium halide has the highest melting point?
explain: Smallest anion F⁻ gives highest lattice enthalpy, hence highest melting point (NaF > NaCl > NaBr > NaI).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In its Lewis structure, which species has a central atom with an incomplete octet?
explain: B in BF₃ has only 6 electrons around it (electron-deficient).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of these atoms cannot expand its octet in compounds?
explain: Period-2 atoms have no vacant d-orbitals, so O (like N) cannot exceed 8 electrons.

prompt: Which of the following is an odd-electron molecule?
explain: NO₂ has 17 valence electrons (odd), leaving an unpaired electron on N.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of σ and π bonds in C₂H₂ respectively:
explain: H–C≡C–H: 2 C–H σ + 1 C–C σ = 3σ; triple bond gives 2π.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In any Lewis structure, the sum of all formal charges equals:
explain: Formal charges add up to the overall charge of the molecule or ion.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Covalent Bond, Lewis Structures & Formal Charge

prompt: Which species contains NO coordinate (dative) bond in its Lewis structure?
explain: NH₄⁺, H₃O⁺, BF₄⁻ each form one dative bond; CH₄ has four normal covalent bonds.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Covalent Bond, Lewis Structures & Formal Charge

prompt: The best Lewis structure has formal charges as small as possible, and any negative charge on the:
explain: Stable structure: minimal formal charges, negative charge on the more electronegative atom.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Covalent Bond, Lewis Structures & Formal Charge

prompt: For H–H covalent bond formation, the bond length corresponds to the point where potential energy is:
explain: Attraction and repulsion balance at the energy minimum, giving the bond length.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Covalent Bond, Lewis Structures & Formal Charge

prompt: In which species does the central atom have 10 electrons in its Lewis structure?
explain: ClF₃: 3 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs on Cl = 10 electrons (expanded octet).
subject: Chemistry
topic: Covalent Bond, Lewis Structures & Formal Charge

prompt: Formal charge formula: FC = V − N − ? (V valence e⁻, N nonbonding e⁻)
explain: Formal charge = valence e⁻ − nonbonding e⁻ − ½(bonding electrons).
subject: Chemistry
topic: Covalent Bond, Lewis Structures & Formal Charge

prompt: Total number of lone pairs on all atoms in CO₂ Lewis structure (O=C=O)?
explain: Each O has 2 lone pairs; carbon has none, so total 4.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Covalent Bond, Lewis Structures & Formal Charge

prompt: Which species has an expanded octet on its central atom?
explain: S in SF₆ has 12 electrons using d-orbitals; others do not exceed 8.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Covalent Bond, Lewis Structures & Formal Charge

prompt: Which species has a central atom with a lone pair and a formal charge of −1 in its best Lewis structure?
explain: NH₂⁻: N has 2 lone pairs and 2 bonds, so 5 − 4 − 2 = −1. In BF₄⁻ the −1 is on B, which has no lone pair.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Covalent Bond, Lewis Structures & Formal Charge

prompt: Pauling's electronegativity scale is based on which property?
explain: Pauling used the excess bond energy of A–B over the mean of A–A and B–B bonds.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: For the same element, which is true of electronegativity as oxidation state increases?
explain: Higher positive charge pulls bonding electrons harder, e.g. Fe³⁺ is more electronegative than Fe²⁺.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which pair correctly shows an exception to 'electronegativity decreases down a group'?
explain: Ga (1.8) is more electronegative than Al (1.5) because of poor d-electron shielding.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which chloride has the greatest covalent character?
explain: Al³⁺ has the highest charge density and polarising power in this set.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: CuCl is more covalent than NaCl even though Cu⁺ and Na⁺ have similar size. Why?
options: Cu⁺ has a pseudo-noble gas (18e⁻) core
Cu⁺ has a noble gas core
Cl⁻ differs in the two salts
explain: The 18-electron d¹⁰ core shields poorly, so Cu⁺ polarises Cl⁻ more than Na⁺ does.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which anion is the most polarisable?
explain: S²⁻ is large and has a high charge, so it is the most easily polarised.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: According to Pauling, an electronegativity difference of about what value gives 50% ionic character?
explain: Δχ ≈ 1.7 corresponds to 50% ionic character; above it the bond is mainly ionic.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which alkali metal halide has the highest ionic character?
explain: Cs is the least electronegative and F the most, so Δχ is the largest and the bond is the most ionic.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Electronegativity of fluorine on the Pauling scale is?
explain: F = 4.0 is the highest value; O = 3.5, Cl = 3.0.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In the Born–Haber cycle, which step is always endothermic for formation of an ionic solid from elements?
explain: Sublimation (atomisation) of a solid metal absorbs energy; lattice formation and ΔH_f are exothermic.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Mulliken's electronegativity is expressed in terms of which two quantities of an atom?
explain: Mulliken defined electronegativity as the average of ionisation energy and electron affinity.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of the following has the highest melting point due to the least covalent character?
explain: Largest cation Ba²⁺ has the lowest polarising power, so BaCl₂ is the most ionic and has the highest m.p.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: SI unit of dipole moment μ = q × d is:
explain: Charge (C) times distance (m) gives C·m. The practical unit is the debye.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of dipole moment of dichlorobenzene isomers:
explain: The angle between the C–Cl dipoles is 60° (ortho), 120° (meta) and 180° (para). Para gives μ = 0.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Correct order of dipole moment among the hydrogen halides:
explain: The dipole moment follows the electronegativity difference, which decreases from F to I.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Chlorobenzene has a lower dipole moment than cyclohexyl chloride because of:
explain: Cl lone-pair delocalisation into the ring and the more electronegative sp² C both reduce the C–Cl moment.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of these is nonpolar (μ = 0) despite polar bonds?
explain: XeF₄ is square planar, so the bond dipoles cancel. SF₄ (see-saw), ClF₃ (T-shaped) and NF₃ (pyramidal) are polar.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which one of these species has a nonzero dipole moment?
explain: SF₄ is see-saw with a lone pair, so it is polar. PCl₅, SF₆ and CCl₄ are symmetric and nonpolar.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Ozone (O₃) has a dipole moment that is:
explain: O₃ is bent with unequal formal charges on the oxygens, so it has a small nonzero μ.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Correct order of dipole moment:
explain: Approximate values: CH₃Cl 1.9 D, CH₂Cl₂ 1.6 D, CHCl₃ 1.0 D, CCl₄ 0 D.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which benzene derivative has zero dipole moment?
explain: 1,3,5-trichlorobenzene is symmetric, so three C–Cl dipoles at 120° cancel.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Two bond moments of 2 D each act at 120° to each other. The resultant is:
explain: The resultant is 2 × 2 × cos 60° = 2 D.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: 1 debye (D) equals approximately:
explain: 1 D = 10⁻¹⁸ esu·cm = 3.336 × 10⁻³⁰ C·m.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: H₂O₂ has a nonzero dipole moment mainly because:
explain: The non-planar skewed geometry stops the O–H dipoles cancelling, giving μ ≈ 2.1 D.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: A molecule containing polar bonds is nonpolar when:
options: The vector sum of bond dipoles is zero
It has an odd number of atoms
It has a lone pair on the central atom
explain: The net dipole moment is the vector sum of the bond moments. Symmetry makes it zero.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Net dipole moment of a molecule depends on:
options: Only the number of lone pairs
explain: The net μ is the vector sum of bond dipoles and lone-pair contributions, so it depends on both magnitude and geometry.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Among CH₄, C₂H₄, C₂H₂ and CH₃OH, the only polar molecule is:
explain: CH₄, C₂H₄ and C₂H₂ are symmetric, so their dipoles cancel. The C–O–H bent geometry makes CH₃OH polar.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: NH₃ has a higher dipole moment than NF₃ mainly because in NF₃:
options: N–F bond dipoles oppose the lone-pair dipole
F has lower electronegativity than H
explain: In NH₃ bond dipoles add to the lone pair; in NF₃ they point opposite to it, so the net is small.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of these molecules has zero dipole moment?
explain: PCl₅ is symmetric trigonal bipyramidal, so the bond dipoles cancel.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Highest dipole moment among CH₃F, CH₃Cl, CH₃Br, CH₃I is of:
explain: Exception: CH₃Cl (1.87 D) > CH₃F (1.85 D) > CH₃Br > CH₃I, since the shorter C–F bond reduces μ.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Dipole moment of H₂O is greater than that of H₂S because:
options: O is more electronegative than S
explain: O–H bonds are more polar (ΔEN larger); H₂O ≈ 1.85 D, H₂S ≈ 0.97 D.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which of the following has zero dipole moment: SO₂, SF₆, H₂S, ClF₃?
explain: SF₆ is perfectly octahedral and symmetric, so bond dipoles cancel; the others are bent or T-shaped.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Correct order of C–O bond length in CO, CO₂ and CO₃²⁻?
explain: C–O bond orders are 3 in CO, 2 in CO₂ and 1.33 in CO₃²⁻. A higher bond order gives a shorter bond.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Bond angle order of NH₃, NF₃ is NH₃ > NF₃. What is the main reason?
options: Bond pair shifted toward N in NH₃ repels more
Bond pair shifted toward F in NF₃ repels more
F atoms are larger than H atoms
NF₃ has two lone pairs on N
explain: In NH₃ bond pairs lie near N, so bp–bp repulsion is greater; in NF₃ they lie near F, giving smaller angle.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Compared with any single canonical structure, the resonance hybrid has
options: Average energy of the canonical forms
explain: Delocalisation lowers the energy; the hybrid is more stable than every contributing structure.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Average C–O bond order in the carbonate ion CO₃²⁻ is
explain: Three equivalent structures: 1 + 1 + 2 = 4 bonds over 3 C–O links → 4/3.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Each O–O bond order in ozone (O₃) is
explain: Two equivalent canonical forms (one single, one double bond) give an average bond order of 1.5.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which species has two C–O bonds of exactly equal length?
explain: Formate is resonance-stabilised, so both C–O bonds are equivalent; formic acid has distinct C=O and C–OH.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Resonance energy is the energy difference between the resonance hybrid and the
explain: It is the extra stabilisation relative to the most stable contributing (canonical) structure.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: All C–C bond lengths in benzene are equal to about
explain: Intermediate between C–C (154 pm) and C=C (134 pm) due to resonance.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Observed heat of hydrogenation of benzene compared with 3 × that of cyclohexene is
explain: Resonance stabilisation of benzene (~150 kJ/mol) makes hydrogenation less exothermic than expected.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Canonical structures contributing to a resonance hybrid are
explain: Only the hybrid exists; resonance forms are imaginary, unlike equilibrium or tautomeric forms.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Resonance stabilisation is greatest when the canonical structures are
explain: Equal-energy (equivalent) forms contribute equally and give the maximum delocalisation stabilisation.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Resonance structures of a molecule must differ only in the position of its:
explain: Canonical forms keep the same atomic arrangement; only the positions of π/lone-pair electrons differ.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry, lone pairs occupy which positions?
explain: Equatorial sites have fewer 90° repulsions, so lone pairs go equatorial (e.g., SF₄, ClF₃, XeF₂).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of repulsion between electron pairs in VSEPR theory?
explain: Lone pairs occupy more space, so lp–lp > lp–bp > bp–bp.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Shape of XeF₆ is (VSEPR, simple prediction)?
explain: 7 electron pairs (6 bp + 1 lp) give a distorted octahedral shape.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Shape of the ICl₄⁻ ion?
explain: 4 bp + 2 lp on I gives octahedral geometry; lone pairs trans, so square planar.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Shape of the ClO₃⁻ ion?
explain: 3 bp + 1 lp on Cl gives tetrahedral geometry, pyramidal shape.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which species is isostructural with XeF₄?
explain: ICl₄⁻ has 4 bp + 2 lp, hence square planar, same as XeF₄.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Shape of the NO₂⁺ ion?
explain: N has 2 bp, no lp (sp), so O=N=O is linear, 180°.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of σ and π bonds in CH₂=CH–C≡N respectively?
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why is a σ bond generally stronger than a π bond between the same two atoms?
explain: Head-on axial overlap is more effective than lateral overlap, so the σ bond is stronger.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Net overlap between an s orbital and a pₓ orbital approaching along the z-axis is:
explain: Positive and negative overlaps cancel by symmetry, so no net bond forms.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which bond type restricts free rotation of atoms about the bond axis?
explain: Rotation would break the lateral overlap of a π bond; σ bonds rotate freely.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In VBT, a covalent bond forms by overlap of orbitals having electrons with:
options: Any spin, one filled and one empty
explain: Half-filled orbitals with opposite spins overlap and pair up, lowering the energy.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The H–F bond arises from which overlap?
explain: Half-filled 1s of H overlaps head-on with a half-filled 2p of F to give a σ bond.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The triple bond in N₂ consists of:
options: One σ (p–p axial) and two π
explain: One axial p–p σ bond, two lateral p–p π bonds (px, py).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of C–C σ bond strength by hybrid orbital overlap?
explain: More s-character means shorter, more directed orbitals, so greater overlap and stronger bond.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Why is a π bond weaker than a σ bond between the same atoms?
explain: Sideways overlap is less effective than head-on overlap, so the π bond is weaker.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Total number of σ and π bonds in ethyne (C₂H₂) respectively:
explain: H–C≡C–H has 2 C–H σ, 1 C–C σ and 2 π bonds: 3σ and 2π.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of σ and π bonds in benzene (C₆H₆) respectively:
explain: 6 C–C σ + 6 C–H σ = 12 σ; the Kekulé structure has 3 C=C π bonds.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: With internuclear axis along z, which overlap forms a π bond?
explain: p_x–p_x (or p_y–p_y) overlap sideways, perpendicular to the z axis, giving a π bond; p_z–p_z is σ.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The nodal plane of a π bond is:
explain: π electron density lies above and below the molecular plane, with a nodal plane containing the internuclear axis.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of σ and π bonds in a molecule of HCN respectively:
explain: H–C≡N: H–C is σ, C≡N is 1σ + 2π, so total 2σ and 2π.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In which of these is rotation about the bond hindered due to the presence of a π bond?
explain: The π bond needs parallel p-orbitals; rotation about C=C would break the π overlap, so it is restricted.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Hybridisation of Xe in XeF₄ and its shape?
explain: 4 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs → sp³d²; lone pairs axial → square planar.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Hybridization Involving s, p, d Orbitals

prompt: Hybridisation of I in the I₃⁻ ion?
explain: 2 bond pairs + 3 lone pairs = 5 electron pairs → sp³d; linear shape.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Hybridization Involving s, p, d Orbitals

prompt: Hybridisation of P in PCl₄⁺ and PCl₆⁻ respectively?
explain: PCl₄⁺: 4 bond pairs → sp³; PCl₆⁻: 6 bond pairs → sp³d².
subject: Chemistry
topic: Hybridization Involving s, p, d Orbitals

prompt: In sp³d hybridisation (trigonal bipyramidal), which d orbital is involved?
explain: sp³d uses d_z²; sp³d² uses d_z² and d_x²−y².
subject: Chemistry
topic: Hybridization Involving s, p, d Orbitals

prompt: Hybridisation of Xe in XeOF₄?
explain: 4 σ(F) + 1 σ(O) + 1 lone pair = 6 pairs → sp³d²; square pyramidal.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Hybridization Involving s, p, d Orbitals

prompt: Which pair of AOs gives zero net overlap along the internuclear (z) axis?
explain: 2s and 2px differ in symmetry about the axis; overlap cancels, so no MO forms.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Bond order of the superoxide ion O₂⁻ is?
explain: O₂⁻ has 17 electrons: Nb = 10, Na = 7, so bond order = 1.5.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: C₂ molecule (ground state) contains which type of bonds?
explain: C₂: σ2s and σ*2s cancel; π2p⁴ gives two π bonds, diamagnetic, bond order 2.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: B₂ is paramagnetic because its two highest electrons are in?
explain: π2p is below σ2p, so two electrons occupy degenerate π2p MOs singly, giving 2 unpaired electrons.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Bond order of N₂⁺ is?
explain: N₂ (BO 3) loses a bonding σ2p electron, so Nb = 9, Na = 4 and BO = 2.5.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Bond order of He₂⁺ is?
explain: Configuration σ1s² σ*1s¹ gives ½(2 − 1) = 0.5, so the ion is stable but weak.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: On going from NO to NO⁺, the bond order and bond length change as?
explain: The electron is removed from π*2p, so BO goes 2.5 → 3 and the bond shortens.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of electrons in antibonding MOs of O₂ is?
explain: σ*2s² and π*2p² give Na = 6 (and σ*1s² makes 8 in the full count). Using the valence-only count Na = 4, so check the convention.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The σ* (antibonding) MO has a nodal plane located where?
options: Perpendicular to the axis, between nuclei
explain: σ* has a node perpendicular to the internuclear axis between the nuclei, where electron density is zero.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: A π bonding MO (from 2px–2px sideways overlap) has a nodal plane that?
options: Lies between nuclei, perpendicular to axis
explain: π MOs have electron density above and below the axis, so the nodal plane contains the molecular axis.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of MOs formed from n combining atomic orbitals is?
explain: MOs formed equal the AOs combined: n/2 bonding and n/2 antibonding.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which diatomic species is isoelectronic with N₂ and has bond order 3?
explain: CO has 14 electrons like N₂; its configuration gives Nb = 10, Na = 4, so BO = 3.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which is NOT a condition for effective LCAO formation of MOs?
options: Same symmetry about the molecular axis
Equal number of electrons in the AOs
explain: LCAO needs similar energy, same symmetry and good overlap; electron count in the AOs is irrelevant.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which diatomic molecule has bond order zero, so it is not stable?
explain: Be₂ has (σ2s)²(σ*2s)², so BO = ½(2 − 2) = 0.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of MO energies for O₂ and F₂ (n > 14 electrons) places which orbital lowest among these?
explain: For O₂, F₂ (no s–p mixing): σ2pz < π2px = π2py < π*2px = π*2py < σ*2pz.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Bond order and magnetic nature of O₂ by MO theory?
explain: O₂ has 10 bonding and 6 antibonding electrons, so B.O. = 2. Two unpaired electrons are in π*2p.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which homonuclear diatomic has σ2p lying ABOVE π2p in energy?
explain: s–p mixing is strong for Z ≤ 7 (Li₂ to N₂), which raises σ2p above π2p. O₂ and F₂ show no inversion.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: C₂ molecule by MO theory: bonding nature?
options: One σ and one π bond, paramagnetic
explain: C₂ has 12 electrons with configuration …(π2p)⁴, giving B.O. 2 with both bonds π and no unpaired electrons.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Bond order of O₂⁻ (superoxide) and its magnetism?
explain: O₂⁻ has 11 electrons in π*2p (π*² π*¹), so B.O. = 1.5 with one unpaired electron.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Peroxide ion O₂²⁻: bond order and magnetic nature?
explain: π*2p is completely filled (4 electrons) so B.O. = ½(10 − 8) = 1 with all electrons paired.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: On ionisation N₂ → N₂⁺, the bond order and bond length change as:
explain: The electron is removed from σ2p, a bonding MO, so B.O. falls from 3 to 2.5 and the bond lengthens.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: On ionisation O₂ → O₂⁺, the bond order and bond length change as:
explain: The electron is removed from π*2p, an antibonding MO, so B.O. rises from 2 to 2.5 and the bond shortens.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The species He₂ has bond order:
explain: He₂ has (σ1s)²(σ*1s)², so Nb = Na and B.O. = 0. The molecule does not exist.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Be₂ molecule by MO theory has bond order:
explain: Be₂ has 8 electrons with σ2s and σ*2s both filled, so Nb = Na and B.O. = 0. Be₂ is not stable.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which one is paramagnetic?
explain: B₂ has two unpaired electrons in the degenerate π2p orbitals. N₂, C₂ and F₂ have all electrons paired.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Magnetic moment (spin only) of O₂ in BM?
explain: O₂ has n = 2 unpaired electrons, so μ = √8 ≈ 2.83 BM.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Bond order of C₂²⁻ is:
explain: C₂²⁻ has 14 electrons, isoelectronic with N₂, so B.O. = 3 and it is diamagnetic.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of electrons in antibonding MOs of O₂ is:
explain: σ*1s² + σ*2s² + π*2p² = 6 antibonding electrons. The 10 bonding electrons give B.O. = 2.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which species has the HOMO of π* type?
explain: The last electrons of O₂ go into π*2p. N₂ has σ2p as HOMO, and C₂ and B₂ have π2p.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which pair has the same bond order of 1?
explain: F₂ has B.O. 1 and O₂²⁻ is isoelectronic with F₂ (18 electrons), so it also has B.O. 1. B₂ is 1 and C₂ is 2.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: N₂ by MO theory: electrons in bonding MOs and bond order?
explain: Nb = 10, Na = 4, so B.O. = ½(10 − 4) = 3; diamagnetic.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Correct MO energy order for O₂ and F₂ (valence, after σ*2s):
explain: Without s–p mixing (Z > 7), σ2p lies below π2p; π*2p lies below σ*2p.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: π2p lies below σ2p in B₂, C₂, N₂ because of:
explain: Small 2s–2p energy gap (Z ≤ 7) gives s–p mixing, which pushes σ2p above π2p.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The two unpaired electrons of B₂ occupy:
options: Two degenerate π2p MOs, one each
explain: Hund's rule: one electron in each of the degenerate π2px and π2py, with parallel spins.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: H₂⁺ has bond order and magnetic nature:
explain: One electron in σ1s gives B.O. = ½ and one unpaired electron.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which species is diamagnetic?
explain: F₂ has all electrons paired (B.O. 1). B₂, O₂⁻ and N₂⁺ each have unpaired electrons.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Bond order of O₂²⁺ is:
explain: O₂²⁺ has 14 electrons, like N₂, so B.O. = 3.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The σ*1s antibonding MO has a nodal plane:
options: Perpendicular to the axis, between the nuclei
explain: Antibonding MO from out-of-phase overlap has zero electron density midway between the nuclei.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Spin-only magnetic moment of O₂⁺ (in BM) is nearest to:
explain: O₂⁺ has one unpaired electron in π*2p, so μ = √3 ≈ 1.73 BM.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which species is isoelectronic with N₂ and has the same bond order of 3?
explain: C₂²⁻ has 14 electrons like N₂, so its bond order is 3. O₂²⁺ also has 14 electrons.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: B₂ is paramagnetic by MOT because its last two electrons occupy
explain: For B₂ (σ2p lies above π2p), the last 2 electrons enter the two degenerate π2p orbitals singly (Hund's rule).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which statement about C₂ is correct by MOT?
options: BO 2, paramagnetic, one σ and one π
BO 3, diamagnetic, one σ and two π
explain: C₂ has 4 electrons in π2p and none in σ2p, so BO = 2, all paired, with two π bonds.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Spin-only magnetic moment of O₂⁻ (superoxide) in BM is
explain: O₂⁻ has one unpaired electron in π*, so n = 1 and μ = √3 ≈ 1.73 BM.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Removing one electron increases the bond order in which species?
explain: O₂ loses an antibonding π* electron, so BO goes from 2 to 2.5. In N₂, C₂ and B₂ a bonding electron is lost.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Number of unpaired electrons in NO⁻ (isoelectronic with O₂) is
explain: NO⁻ has 16 electrons, like O₂. Two unpaired electrons sit in π* orbitals, BO = 2.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Bond order of O₂²⁺ by MOT is
explain: O₂²⁺ has 14 electrons, isoelectronic with N₂. BO = (10 − 4)/2 = 3.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which species is paramagnetic by MOT: C₂, N₂, Be₂, B₂?
explain: B₂ has two unpaired electrons in degenerate π2p orbitals (σ2p lies above π2p for Z ≤ 7).
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In the electron-sea model, a metallic bond is the attraction between:
options: Shared electron pairs between two atoms
explain: Positive metal kernels are held together by a sea of mobile, delocalised valence electrons.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Electrical conductivity of metals is mainly due to:
explain: The electron sea moves under an applied potential, carrying current.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Malleability and ductility of metals arise because the metallic bond is:
explain: Layers slide over each other and the electron sea readjusts without breaking the bonding.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Metallic lustre is due to:
options: Free electrons absorbing and re-emitting light
explain: Mobile electrons absorb visible light and re-emit it, giving a shiny surface.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: With rise in temperature, the electrical conductivity of a metal:
explain: Greater kernel vibration scatters the electrons and increases resistance.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which has the strongest metallic bonding among Na, Mg, Al?
explain: More valence electrons and smaller size strengthen the bond; Al has 3 electrons and the smallest size.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which alkali metal has the highest melting point?
explain: Metallic bond strength falls down the group as size increases, so Li is highest.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Transition metals generally have high melting points because:
explain: Both ns and (n−1)d electrons are delocalised, so the bonds are stronger.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Metallic bond strength increases with:
options: More valence electrons and smaller kernel size
More valence electrons and larger kernel size
Fewer valence electrons and smaller kernel size
Lower nuclear charge and larger kernel size
explain: More delocalised electrons and a smaller kernel give a stronger electrostatic attraction in the metal.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which metal is liquid at room temperature due to very weak metallic bonding?
explain: Hg has a stable filled 4f¹⁴5d¹⁰6s² core; its 6s² electrons are held tightly, so its metallic bonding is weak and it is a liquid.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Ice floats on water because H-bonding in ice gives a structure that is:
explain: Tetrahedral H-bonded open cage in ice has voids, so density is lower than liquid water.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Water shows maximum density at which temperature?
explain: Up to 4 °C the H-bonded cages collapse and density rises; above 4 °C thermal expansion dominates.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Correct boiling point order of group 15 hydrides:
explain: NH₃ is anomalously high due to H-bonding; the rest rise with size and van der Waals forces.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of hydrogen bond strength:
explain: Strength follows electronegativity of the donor atom: F > O > N.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: KHF₂ exists but KHCl₂ does not, because:
options: F forms strong H-bonds in HF₂⁻
KCl is more ionic than KF
explain: HF₂⁻ is stabilised by strong F–H···F⁻ hydrogen bonding; Cl is too weak an H-bond acceptor.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Solid boric acid, H₃BO₃, has a layered structure held together by:
explain: Planar B(OH)₃ units are linked by H-bonds into layers, which gives a slippery feel.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Acetic acid in benzene shows molar mass about 120 because it:
explain: Two –COOH groups pair through two O–H···O bonds, so the dimer's mass (120) is observed.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Ethanol boils higher than dimethyl ether (same molar mass) because ethanol has:
explain: Ethanol has an O–H group, giving intermolecular H-bonds; the ether has none.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: H-bond extent in water states: order of H-bonding magnitude is
explain: H-bonding is maximum in the solid state and least in the gaseous state.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: The α-helix of proteins is stabilised mainly by:
explain: Backbone N–H and C=O groups form intramolecular H-bonds that hold the helix.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Intramolecular H-bonding in a molecule generally makes its water solubility:
explain: The H-bond is internal, so the molecule cannot bond with water; o-nitrophenol is less soluble than the para isomer.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Solid HF has which structure due to H-bonding?
explain: F–H···F links give zig-zag polymeric chains in solid HF.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Order of electronegativity of carbon in different hybrid states?
explain: More s-character holds the bonding electrons closer to the nucleus, so electronegativity rises: sp (50%) > sp² > sp³.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: SnCl₂ is a solid, while SnCl₄ is a volatile liquid. Which Fajans' factor explains this?
options: Higher charge on Sn in SnCl₄ → more covalent
Higher charge on Sn in SnCl₂ → more covalent
Smaller Cl⁻ in SnCl₄ → more covalent
explain: Sn⁴⁺ has greater polarising power (higher charge, smaller size) than Sn²⁺, so SnCl₄ is covalent and volatile.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In the crossed-arrow notation (↦) for a bond dipole, the arrow head points toward the:
options: Atom with the larger atomic radius
explain: The arrow runs from the δ⁺ (less electronegative) atom to the δ⁻ (more electronegative) atom; the cross marks the positive end.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which has a nonzero dipole moment: CO₂, CS₂, COS, or CCl₄?
explain: COS (O=C=S) is linear but unsymmetrical, so the C=O and C=S dipoles do not cancel.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: A π bond between two atoms can form only when the atoms are already joined by which bond?
explain: π overlap is lateral and needs the atoms held at bonding distance by a σ bond; a double bond is 1σ + 1π.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which orbitals take part in forming π bonds in sp² and sp hybridised atoms?
explain: Hybrid orbitals form σ bonds; the leftover unhybridised p orbitals overlap sideways to form π bonds.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Total number of nodal planes in a π* (antibonding) MO formed from 2px–2px overlap is?
explain: π* has the plane containing the axis plus a plane perpendicular to the axis between the nuclei.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Among σ*1s, σ2s, π2px and σ2pz, which MO has the lowest energy?
explain: 1s-based MOs lie far below n = 2 MOs; σ*1s is still lower than σ2s.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In an antibonding MO, the electron density is mainly located where?
explain: Antibonding MO has low or zero density between nuclei, so repulsion between nuclei increases.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In LCAO, the antibonding MO is obtained from AOs ψA and ψB by which combination?
explain: Bonding MO = ψA + ψB (in phase); antibonding MO = ψA − ψB (out of phase), giving a node between nuclei.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Spin-only magnetic moment of B₂ (two unpaired electrons) in BM is nearest to:
explain: B₂ has 2 unpaired electrons in π2p, so μ = √8 ≈ 2.83 BM.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Bond order of NO molecule by MOT is
explain: 11 valence electrons: N_b = 8, N_a = 3, so BO = 2.5, with one unpaired electron in π*.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Bond order of NO⁻ (isoelectronic with O₂) by MOT is
explain: 12 valence electrons: N_b = 8, N_a = 4, so BO = 2, with 2 unpaired electrons in π*.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: F₂ by MOT: bond order and magnetic behaviour?
explain: F₂ has 8 bonding and 6 antibonding valence electrons, so BO = 1 and all π* orbitals are filled, hence diamagnetic.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which property of metals is best explained by the non-directional, delocalised metallic bond acting as a 'glue' on layer slip?
options: Metals do not fracture when layers slide
explain: Delocalised electrons keep bonding intact when layers slip, so metals do not fracture.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Metals are good conductors of heat mainly because of:
explain: Mobile electrons carry kinetic energy rapidly through the metal lattice.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: In DNA, the base pairs A–T and G–C are joined by how many H-bonds respectively?
explain: A=T has 2 H-bonds; G≡C has 3 H-bonds, so G–C pairs are stronger.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which is steam volatile because of intramolecular H-bonding?
explain: o-Nitrophenol is chelated, so it has no intermolecular association and is steam volatile; p-isomer is associated.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Correct boiling point order of hydrogen halides:
explain: HF is anomalously high due to H-bonding; the rest rise with size (dispersion forces): HI > HBr > HCl.
subject: Chemistry

prompt: Which molecule cannot form H-bonds with its own molecules?
explain: Dimethyl ether has no H on O (no O–H bond), so no self-association; the others have O–H, N–H or F–H.
subject: Chemistry
